old_caption: The video captures a serene scene of a cloudy sky with the sun prominently positioned near the center, casting a bright light that contrasts sharply with the surrounding darker clouds. A distinct halo effect is visible around the sun, caused by ice crystals in high-altitude cirrus clouds. Below the sky, a row of buildings is visible as silhouettes, with some showing flat roofs and others sloped ones. A few utility poles and wires run horizontally across the frame, adding to the urban landscape. The overall atmosphere is calm and somewhat overcast, suggesting either early morning or late afternoon. A watermark is present in the top-left corner, and the camera exhibits a very slight, slow drift or pan throughout the clip.

caption: The video captures a hazy gray sky above dark rooftops, with power lines slanting across the lower frame. The sun sits near the center as a bright white disc, flanked by two pale side glows at the same height. A faint circular band surrounds the sun, while the two side patches remain aligned with it throughout the clip. Thin cloud layers drift slowly across the sky, changing the brightness and texture around the halo without moving the sun or its side glows. The rooftops and wires shift slightly to one side as the view drifts, while the sky patterns keep evolving overhead. The visible scene presents a stable sun-dog display under moving cloud cover, with the halo and side glows holding their positions as the thin veil shifts slowly.

An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.
